entries.note: A 'firm, reliable foundation' has no shared operational meaning or specified use here.

entries.test: Published experiment transcripts would establish whether GPT-3 produced the reported biologically erroneous continuation under the stated prompt.
entries.note: Marcus endorses this passage from his own joint work with Davis. The biological-failure characterization has a concrete referent in the juice example.
The proposition adds a firm statistical explanation where the preceding source sentence says 'presumably.' Understanding these concepts has no agreed test in this passage.
The passage supplies no shared criterion for when statistics have fully substituted for 'deeper understanding.'

entries.test: Public evaluations and controlled training studies could establish whether historically available image generators struggled with rare compositional requests because of their reliance on statistical frequency.
entries.note: The concrete claim connects request rarity with observable generation failures.

entries.test: Public training-data audits and controlled experiments varying left-handed drawing examples could establish whether insufficient relevant training data caused the reported failures.
entries.note: The proposition expands a rebuttal about one system into a general causal claim about image generators. Google Images availability alone does not establish what a system was taught.

entries.test: Public controlled comparisons of ordinary and reformulated left-handed drawing prompts could distinguish failures to interpret the request from inability to render the requested image.
entries.note: Successful reformulations provide an observable basis for testing the proposed explanation.

entries.test: Public prompt-response records and controlled handedness evaluations could establish whether the reported guitarist error followed common statistical associations despite the linguistic request.
entries.note: The source explicitly describes this example as not involving drawing; it does not support attribution to image generators. Statistical frequency winning out is an explanation of the error.
Neither statistics 'outweighing' understanding nor a 'shaky' foundation supplies a shared criterion for settling this broad conclusion.
